verifications.claim: Artemis II mission launched on April 1, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'NASA’s Artemis II mission is set to launch on April 1, 2026.'; R3: post-launch coverage implying April 1; R4: 'At 6:35 p.m. EDT, the Artemis 2 mission successfully lifted off'; R5: 'launched from Florida to the moon on Wednesday (April 1)'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm launch on April 1, 2026.

verifications.claim: Artemis II mission is a 10-day crewed flight.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '10-day odyssey'; R2: '10-day mission'; R3: '10 days'; R6: 'approximately 10-day test flight'
verifications.reasoning: All sources explicitly state 10-day mission duration.

verifications.claim: Artemis II mission tests the Orion spacecraft.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'tests of Orion’s life-support systems'; R2: 'performing critical tests of various systems'; R7: 'first full-up test of NASA's deep-space exploration system with astronauts'
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly describe testing Orion systems.

verifications.claim: Artemis II mission tests the SLS rocket.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'first crewed test mission that successfully flew SLS'; R7: 'first to fly astronauts aboard the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket'
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly first crewed SLS flight, implying tests.

verifications.claim: Artemis II mission involves flight around the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'journey around the moon’s far side'; R2: 'looping around the far side of the Moon'
verifications.reasoning: All describe lunar flyby around far side.

verifications.claim: Astronauts on Artemis II mission are Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Hammock Koch, Jeremy Hansen'; identical in others
verifications.reasoning: Exact crew listed in multiple sources.

verifications.claim: Artemis II mission marks the first human deep-space mission in over 50 years.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'first time astronauts return to the vicinity of the moon in more than 50 years'; R4: 'first time humans have headed to the Moon since Apollo 17 in 1972'
verifications.reasoning: Directly stated as first since Apollo 17 (1972).

verifications.claim: Space Launch System (SLS) lifted off from Kennedy Space Center's Launch Complex 39B at 6:35 p.m. EDT on April 1, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'At 6:35 p.m. EDT, the Artemis 2 mission successfully lifted off from the Kennedy Space Center at Cape Canaveral' (context LC39B); 'Launch Pad 39B'
verifications.reasoning: Exact time, location, and date match.

verifications.claim: SLS successfully inserted the Orion spacecraft into Earth orbit.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'SLS produces... boost Orion to a highly elliptical Earth orbit'; R6: 'after Artemis II lifts off... will be in space'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm SLS places Orion in Earth orbit.

verifications.claim: On Day 1 of Artemis II mission, following separation, the crew spent 90 minutes in a high Earth elliptical orbit.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R8: 'Orion will spend 90-minutes in its initial orbit, before the second stage fires... to a high Earth elliptical orbit'
verifications.reasoning: R8 directly states 90 minutes initial orbit post-separation.

verifications.claim: On Day 1 of Artemis II mission, the crew tested life support systems.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'tests of Orion’s life-support systems'; R6: 'testing systems like the potable water dispenser... toilet, and... carbon dioxide'
verifications.reasoning: Explicit Day 1 life support tests.

verifications.claim: On Day 1 of Artemis II mission, the crew deployed solar arrays.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'Orion has unfurled four nearly 23-foot-long wings... solar arrays' (T+26min Day1); R8: 'Orion will then deploy its four solar arrays'
verifications.reasoning: Confirmed on Day 1 post-launch.

verifications.claim: On Day 2 of Artemis II mission, Interim Cryogenic Propulsion Stage (ICPS) fires.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R4: ICPS fires perigee/apogee Day1 (T+49min, etc.); R6: ICPS fires on FD1 for orbit raises
verifications.reasoning: ICPS burns occur on Day 1, not Day 2; Day 2 is Orion TLI.

verifications.claim: Interim Cryogenic Propulsion Stage (ICPS) boosts the crew from Earth orbit onto a figure-eight trajectory toward the Moon.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R1: 'day two, Orion will perform its “translunar injection burn”'; R6: 'TLI... done by Orion’s main engine'
verifications.reasoning: TLI to translunar/figure-8 by Orion ESM, not ICPS (which does Earth orbit raises).

verifications.claim: Days 2-4 of Artemis II mission involve outbound transit to the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'On day two... propel... to the moon... smaller burns over the following two days'; R8: 'Days 2 - 4: Outbound transit'
verifications.reasoning: Direct match for outbound transit Days 2-4.

verifications.claim: During days 2-4 of Artemis II mission, the crew refines the spacecraft's systems.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R1: 'smaller burns... to correct their path'; R6: 'outbound trajectory correction... checkouts and demonstrations'
verifications.reasoning: Corrections and checkouts support refining, but broader terms used.

verifications.claim: On Day 5 of Artemis II mission, Orion enters the Moon’s sphere of influence.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'day five, Orion will slip into the moon’s gravitational sphere'; R6: 'Flight Day 5 Orion will enter the lunar sphere'
verifications.reasoning: Exact match.

verifications.claim: On Day 5 of Artemis II mission, Orion begins swing around the far side of the Moon.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Day five... sphere... Day six... far side'; R6: FD5 enter SOI, FD6 closest
verifications.reasoning: Swing begins after Day 5 entry, but Day 6 specified for far side.

verifications.claim: On Day 6 of Artemis II mission, the crew flies to the far side of the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Day six will take... to the far side'
verifications.reasoning: Direct statement.

verifications.claim: On Day 6 of Artemis II mission, the crew momentarily loses contact with Earth.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'briefly outside of radio contact'; R6: 'lose communication... 30-50 minutes as they pass behind the Moon'
verifications.reasoning: Explicit loss of contact on Day 6.

verifications.claim: On Day 6 of Artemis II mission, the crew performs manual close-proximity flight maneuvers.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R4: 'proximity operations demonstration' on Day 1 with ICPS; R6: Day 6 lunar observations/photos
verifications.reasoning: Prox ops on Day 1, Day 6 is lunar flyby observations.

verifications.claim: On Day 6 of Artemis II mission, the crew takes images of the lunar surface.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'taking photos of the moon... images of “Earthrise”'; R6: 'taking photos and videos of the Moon'
verifications.reasoning: Directly stated for Day 6.

verifications.claim: Days 7-9 of Artemis II mission are return trip to Earth.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'after lunar encounter... next few days prepping... homecoming'; R8: 'Days 7 - 10: Return'; R6: FD7-9 return corrections/prep
verifications.reasoning: Return phase covers Days 7-10, including 7-9.

verifications.claim: On Day 10 of Artemis II mission, the crew module separates from the service module.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'the smaller crew module will detach from the rest of Orion'; R6: 'crew module will separate from the service module'
verifications.reasoning: Exact on Day 10.

verifications.claim: On Day 10 of Artemis II mission, the crew module performs high-speed high-heat re-entry through Earth’s atmosphere.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'atmospheric reentry... 3,000 degrees Fahrenheit'; R6: 'through Earth’s atmosphere... 3,000 degrees Fahrenheit'
verifications.reasoning: Direct Day 10 reentry description.

verifications.claim: On Day 10 of Artemis II mission, the crew module splashes down in the Pacific Ocean.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'splashdown in the Pacific Ocean'; R6: 'splashdown in the Pacific Ocean'
verifications.reasoning: Explicit Day 10 Pacific splashdown.

verifications.claim: Backup launch windows for Artemis II mission were available on April 2-6, 2026, and April 30, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'next available launch window dates... April 2... April 3... April 4... April 5... April 6... April 30'
verifications.reasoning: Exact dates listed.

verifications.claim: Backup launch opportunities for Artemis II mission were at Adler Planetarium.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.evidence: No relevant content found
verifications.reasoning: No sources mention Adler Planetarium as launch site; R2 is Adler blog but launch from KSC.
